system_overview: This specification models the Boyer-Moore majority vote algorithm, an efficient single-pass algorithm that identifies the only candidate element in a sequence that could hold a strict majority (appearing in more than half the positions). The algorithm was originally published by R.S. Boyer and J.S. Moore in a 1981 technical report and later in print in 1991. It uses constant extra space beyond the input sequence.
actors_and_components: The system has a single sequential actor that scans through an input sequence of values from a finite nonempty set. There are no concurrent processes or distributed components.
state_variables: The system tracks four pieces of state: (1) the input sequence of values, which is chosen nondeterministically at initialization and never modified, (2) a position index indicating the next element to examine, (3) the current candidate for majority element, and (4) a counter representing a lower bound on how many more times the candidate has appeared compared to other elements in the portion scanned so far.
initial_state: The input sequence is chosen nondeterministically from all possible sequences over the value set. The position index starts at the first position. The candidate is chosen nondeterministically from the value set. The counter starts at zero.
actions: There is one transition that executes when the position index has not yet passed the end of the sequence. Three cases arise: (1) If the counter is zero, the current element becomes the new candidate and the counter is set to one. (2) If the counter is nonzero and the current element matches the candidate, the counter is incremented. (3) If the counter is nonzero and the current element differs from the candidate, the counter is decremented. In all cases, the position index advances by one and the input sequence remains unchanged.
safety_properties: The main correctness property is: once the scan is complete (the position index exceeds the sequence length), if any value occurs in a strict majority of positions in the sequence, then that value must equal the current candidate. An inductive invariant supports this: (a) the counter never exceeds the number of times the candidate has appeared so far, (b) twice the excess occurrences of the candidate beyond the counter does not exceed the number of non-candidate positions scanned, and (c) for every non-candidate value, twice its occurrence count does not exceed the number of non-candidate positions scanned. A type correctness invariant ensures all variables remain in their expected domains.
liveness_properties: Under weak fairness, the algorithm eventually completes its scan of the entire sequence (the position index eventually exceeds the sequence length).
model_bounds: The value set and sequence length bounds are provided as model-checking parameters. A companion model-checking module defines a set of three distinct values and bounds the sequence length.
additional_assumptions: The specification assumes the value set is nonempty. Weak fairness is assumed on the next-state action. The input sequence is modeled as a variable (rather than a constant) to allow the model checker to verify the algorithm for all sequences up to a bounded size.
